analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The sole changed line (head 2371, per the patch hunk) adds a troubleshooting-table row. It says a cold load can be refused (503 or insufficient-memory) while an idle model is resident, because that slot holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. Held slots are excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel), and their weights get no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). The referenced source file ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift and the model-autopilot.md anchor were not supplied, so I could not check that the described behavior matches the code.

The supplied units (head lines 416-1227) are unchanged surrounding documentation. I examined them for context: Nemotron Super slot, GLM5Next, calibration, prefix cache and SSD stage text. Nothing in them is modified by this PR. The doc-only change alters no code or controls, no trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011) and no assets (A-001, A-003, A-004). It adds no attack surface and does not affect T-041 (SSD prefix cache) or any App Attest authorization behavior.

One availability point for the next pass: if Autopilot holds can block eviction and starve cold loads, that is a possible DoS-style interaction. It is documented as intended behavior and is pre-existing, not a regression introduced here. The hold-expiry and ownership semantics in the Autopilot source are outside the supplied evidence. I raise no finding and request no deeper review.
